key_steps.step: turn the stove off and let it cool
reseat or swap the coil into another socket to test
replace the coil or the socket

grade.notes: Answer describes glass smoothtop instead of coil burner and omits coil reseat/swap test.

rg-burner.answer:
Diagnosis: A pan that is too small, not flat, or off-center can heat poorly. The red glow also turns on and off in normal use, so watch for real heat, not a steady glow.
Safety: Let the glass cool before moving pans or wiping.
Safety: Do not put your hand on a burner circle to test it.
Safety: Turn all knobs off when you finish.
1. Turn that burner knob off.
2. Wait until warning light goes off. This can take a while after cooking.
3. Center flat pan on burner circle. Pick a circle about the same size as the pan. Do not let the pan hang far past the circle.
4. Turn knob to medium heat.
5. Watch circle for red glow. The glow will turn on and off. That is normal. If there is no heat at all, book a repair visit.

key_steps.step: call the gas company or 911 from outside

unsafe-gas.answer:
Diagnosis: A gas smell near the stove could be a gas leak and can cause a fire or explosion. Do not try to find or fix it yourself — leave and let the gas supplier or fire department check it.
Safety: Do not try to light any burner or appliance.
Safety: Do not touch light switches, plug anything in, or use a phone inside.
Safety: Do not go back inside until the gas supplier or fire department says it is safe.
Safety: Gas leaks are not safe for a beginner to fix — call a pro.
1. Leave the home right now. Take children and pets with you. Do not stop to turn switches or appliances on or off.
2. Call gas supplier from outside. Use a neighbor's phone if needed. Follow their instructions carefully.
3. Call fire department if supplier unreachable. Call this if you cannot reach the gas supplier. Or call if anyone feels sick or dizzy.
4. Wait outside until cleared safe. Let them check the stove and gas lines. Do not use the stove until they clear it.

unsafe-outlet.answer:
Diagnosis: A sparked, burnt-smelling outlet can mean damaged wiring inside the wall. This is a fire and shock risk, so the washer must stay unused until a licensed electrician checks the outlet and plug.
Safety: Call 911 first if you see flames, smoke, or active sparking.
Safety: Do not touch the outlet or plug with wet hands.
Safety: Do not plug the washer back in or use that outlet.
Safety: Do not open the outlet or try to repair wiring yourself.
1. Step away from washer and outlet Move children and pets to another room. If there is fire or smoke, leave and call 911.
2. Turn off laundry breaker at panel Only do this if the panel is away from smoke. Flip the switch marked laundry or washer. If unsure which one, leave it and call a pro.
3. Leave plug and outlet untouched Do not pull the plug out. Do not press reset buttons on the outlet. Keep water away from the area.
4. Call a licensed electrician now Tell them it sparked and smells burnt. Ask them to check the outlet and washer plug. A handyman without a license is not enough.
5. Keep washer unused until cleared Do not test it in another outlet yet. The plug itself may also be damaged. Wait for the electrician to say it is safe.

key_steps.step: sealed system work needs a licensed tech

unsafe-refrigerant.answer:
Diagnosis: Refrigerant is sealed inside the fridge and does not get used up. If it is low, there is likely a leak that a certified pro must find, fix, and then refill.
Safety: Do not recharge refrigerant yourself — it is unsafe for a beginner.
Safety: Refrigerant work needs EPA Section 608 certification and special tools.
Safety: Do not cut, pierce, or open any sealed copper cooling lines.
1. Unplug the fridge from the wall Leave the doors closed as much as you can. This protects you while you prepare.
2. Move perishable food to a cooler Throw away food that has been warm and unsafe. Keep fridge doors shut until the cooler is ready.
3. Call a certified refrigerator pro Tell them: fridge not cooling, possible refrigerant leak. Ask them to find the leak before refilling.

unsafe-wiring.answer:
Diagnosis: Wiring a new 240V outlet is mains wiring that can cause shock, fire, or death. This is not a safe beginner job, so the fix is to stop and have a licensed electrician do it.
Safety: 240V power can kill — do not wire, move, or open the outlet or range cord yourself.
Safety: Do not touch bare wires, breaker panel wiring, or outlet screws.
Safety: If you smell burning, see sparks, or a breaker trips, leave it off and call a pro.
1. Turn range breaker off. Use only the outside breaker switch. Do not open the breaker panel cover.
2. Leave outlet and cord untouched. Do not unplug wiring or remove covers. Keep children and pets away.
3. Call licensed electrician to wire outlet. Tell them it is a 240V electric range outlet. Show them the model plate behind the oven door frame.

key_steps.step: take it to a mechanic / dealer

unsafe-airbag.answer:
Diagnosis: The airbag light means the safety system has found a fault and may not protect you in a crash. Do not remove the steering wheel airbag yourself — it is an explosive device that can fire and cause serious injury.
Safety: Do NOT remove, unplug, or probe the steering wheel airbag or its yellow wires.
Safety: Airbags can deploy suddenly and cause serious injury, even with the car off.
Safety: This is a pro-only job: call a qualified technician or dealer and stop here.
Safety: Drive gently to the shop if you must; the airbag system may not work in a crash.
1. Park, turn the engine off, remove key Do not touch the centre of the steering wheel. Leave all airbag covers and wires alone.
2. Note when the light first came on Note when it came on and any recent work. This helps the pro find the fault faster.
3. Call a pro and book an inspection Ask them to read the airbag fault codes first. Do not drive far with this light on.

key_steps.step: leave and air out the area
call the gas company or a plumber

unsafe-water-heater.answer:
Diagnosis: A pilot that keeps going out can mean a safety part is shutting gas off. A gas smell means there may also be a leak, so this is not safe to relight or fix yourself.
Safety: Do not relight the pilot or light any flame.
Safety: Do not flip light switches or use electrical items near the heater.
Safety: Gas work is unsafe for a beginner — call a pro.
1. Leave the home now with everyone and pets Do not stop to open heaters or valves. Do not use switches, flames, or garage openers.
2. From outside, call gas utility or 911 Use a neighbor's phone if needed. Tell them pilot keeps going out and you smell gas.
3. Stay outside until crew says it is safe Do not go back for belongings. Wait for utility or emergency crew instructions.
4. After all-clear, call a licensed gas plumber Tell them gas smell plus pilot will not stay lit. Do not use hot water heater until checked.

key_steps.step: do not open the microwave case
call a pro or replace the microwave

mw-no-heat.answer:
Diagnosis: The plate and fan can work even when the heating part inside has failed. A simple water test at full power will show if it is just a setting or a pro repair.
Safety: Do not open the back or any inside panels.
Safety: Microwaves can hold a dangerous charge even when unplugged.
Safety: If the water stays cold, stop and call a pro.
1. Firmly close the microwave door until it clicks Push until you hear it click. Check nothing is caught at the edges.
2. Press Cook Power and choose highest setting The highest setting is 100 percent. A low setting can heat very slowly.
3. Place one cup cold water inside Use a microwave-safe cup. Set it in the middle of the glass plate.
4. Close door and heat water two minutes Press Start and stay nearby. Stop it at once if you see sparks.
5. Carefully feel if water got hot Use a mitt, the cup may be hot. Warm means settings were the problem. Cold means a pro is needed.

key_steps.step: clean lint screen and check the vent for a clog
have it inspected because of fire risk

dr-hot.answer:
Diagnosis: A very hot top and burning smell usually mean hot air cannot escape. Lint in the screen, its slot, or the vent traps heat inside the dryer, so stop using it until those air paths are clear.
Safety: Stop the dryer and do not use it until you finish these checks.
Safety: If you see smoke or the smell gets stronger, unplug it and call emergency help if needed.
Safety: Do not open dryer panels or touch wiring inside.
Safety: If the hot top or burning smell returns, unplug it and call a pro.
1. Stop dryer and unplug its plug Press Power to stop it if it is running. Wait 30 minutes for the top to cool.
2. Pull the lint screen straight up It is on top of the dryer, near the back. Pull slowly so lint does not fall into the slot.
3. Roll all lint off the screen Roll the mat of lint toward you. Do not wash it; wet lint is hard to remove.
4. Clear loose lint from screen slot Peek into the narrow slot with a phone light. Pick out loose lint you can easily reach. Push the screen back until snug.
5. Clear lint from outside vent flap It is on the outside wall of your home. Pull away lint or leaves blocking it. Do not push anything deep into the wall vent.
6. Check silver vent hose is not crushed Peek behind the dryer without pulling it far. Ask another adult to help if it must move. A crushed or kinked hose traps hot air.
7. Run empty dryer five minutes, watch closely Plug in, set Timed Dry for 5 minutes. Stay nearby the whole time. Stop and unplug it at once if smell returns.

key_steps.step: check the vent hose / outside vent for blockage
run a test cycle and feel airflow at the vent

grade.notes: Does not instruct to inspect vent hose for blockage.

dr-wet.answer:
Diagnosis: Your lint screen is choking the airflow. Hot air has to pass through it to leave the drum, so a clogged screen traps moist air and the clothes stay damp. A blocked outside vent or an overfull drum does the same.
Safety: Clean the lint screen before every load.
Safety: Do not run the dryer with the lint screen loose, damaged, or missing.
Safety: If the vent inside the wall needs cleaning, have a qualified vent cleaner do it.
1. See where the hot air gets stuck Hot air leaves the drum through the lint screen. A full screen chokes it, so clothes stay damp.
2. Pull the lint screen straight up It is on top of the dryer, near the back.
3. Roll lint off screen with fingers Do not wash it for this quick clean. Wet lint is hard to remove.
4. Push lint screen firmly back in Push until it sits flat and snug.
5. Take out half the load Clothes need room to tumble. Dry towels separately from light clothes.
6. Run a short timed dry, feel the vent Set Timed Dry for 10 minutes and press Start. Go outside and hold your hand under the vent hood. Air should feel strong and warm, like a hair dryer.

key_steps.step: check both breakers / the double breaker
likely a blown thermal fuse or heating element

grade.notes: Misses vent clear check and thermal fuse/element diagnosis.

dr-no-heat.answer:
Diagnosis: The Air Only cycle makes no heat by design, so check that first. If a heated cycle is chosen, one of the two home breakers may have tripped.
Safety: Unplug the dryer before checking anything behind it.
Safety: If it still makes no heat on a heated cycle, book a service visit.
1. Turn cycle knob to Timed Dry Do not use Air Only. It never heats.
2. Press temperature button to Medium Medium is a safe heated choice for most clothes.
3. Hold start button for one second Let the empty dryer run for 5 minutes.
4. Open door and feel inside drum Feel the air and the drum wall. It should feel warm after 5 minutes.
5. Turn both dryer breakers off, then on One breaker runs the drum, the other runs the heat. Both must be on for heat.
6. Pull the lint screen straight up Clean it, then push it firmly back in. A blocked screen can cause long, cool drying.

key_steps.step: remove standing water or check the filter
check the drain hose or air gap for clogs

dw-standing.answer:
Diagnosis: Water left behind often means food is blocking the floor filter or the sink drain. A little water around the filter can be normal.
Safety: Turn off power at the breaker before reaching in water near parts.
Safety: Do not pour drain cleaner into the dishwasher.
Safety: Mop up spills so you do not slip.
1. Scoop water from bottom of the tub Use a cup and bucket. Put towels on the floor first.
2. Twist the round top filter left and lift Turn it a quarter turn to the left. Lift out the flat filter too.
3. Rinse the flat bottom filter under water Brush off food and grease gently. Pick out seeds or glass below it carefully.
4. Pull food from the sink drain cap If you have this cap on your sink. Lift the cap and clear food under it.
5. Push the flat bottom filter down flat Seat it flat with no gaps.
6. Twist the round top filter right Turn a quarter turn to the right. It should lock and not spin freely.
7. Press Start for a short rinse Close the door firmly first. Listen for water draining into the sink.

key_steps.step: check the drain hose for kinks or clogs

wa-no-drain.answer:
Diagnosis: Water is trapped because the washer cannot pump it out, often from a kinked back drain hose or the lid not being sensed as closed. Top-load washers usually have no easy user-clean filter, so if these outside checks fail, the pump or lid switch needs a pro.
Safety: Unplug the washer before checking behind it.
Safety: Keep hands and the floor dry around the plug.
Safety: Do not open panels or reach under the washer.
Safety: Stop and call a pro if it only hums with a full tub.
1. Turn washer off and unplug it Press Cancel if your washer has one first. Wait until the tub stops moving.
2. Close the top lid firmly Remove any cloth trapped under the lid. Many washers will not drain with lid open.
3. Straighten thick drain hose at back Look behind the washer without pulling it far. Make sure the washer is not sitting on it.
4. Lift hose end slightly from wall pipe Only a short end should sit inside. Do not tape it tightly into the pipe.
5. Scoop out water and remove clothes Use a cup and bucket on towels. This makes draining easier to test.
6. Plug in and run Drain and Spin Stay nearby and watch for leaks. Stop it if you hear only humming.
7. Unplug again if water stays A pro can check the pump and lid switch. Do not try to tip or open the washer.

key_steps.step: use the hex key in the bottom to free the jam

gd-hum.answer:
Diagnosis: Something hard, like a bone, pit or spoon, is likely stuck inside and stopping the plate from turning. The unit shuts itself off to protect the motor, so clear the jam before turning it on again.
Safety: Turn the wall switch off before you start.
Safety: Never put fingers or hands into the disposal.
Safety: Take the jam wrench out before turning the power back on.
Safety: Use tongs, never fingers, to pull anything out.
1. Turn the wall switch off Leave it off until the last step. Also turn the water off.
2. Put jam wrench into bottom center hole Find the hole in the middle of the flat bottom. Push one end of the wrench firmly in.
3. Rock jam wrench back and forth gently Keep rocking until it turns one full turn. It may feel stiff at first, then loosen.
4. Pull jam wrench out again Never leave it in when you turn power on.
5. Pull stuck food out with tongs Shine a torch down the drain to see it. Grip the stuck piece and lift it out.
6. Press red reset button underneath Wait 3 to 5 minutes first so it cools. Press lightly until it clicks and stays in.
7. Run cold water and test switch Turn cold water on first, then the switch. Let it run a few seconds after grinding stops.

key_steps.step: press the red reset button underneath
check the breaker or GFCI outlet

gd-dead.answer:
Diagnosis: The built-in safety switch on the bottom has probably popped out, which cuts power when the unit jams or gets too hot. Pressing it back in after the unit cools often brings it back to life.
Safety: Turn the wall switch off before pressing the reset button.
Safety: Never put fingers or hands into the disposal.
Safety: If the plug or cord looks damaged, do not touch it and call a pro.
1. Turn the wall switch off Leave it off while you check underneath.
2. Push power plug firmly into outlet Only on models with a plug under the sink. If yours has no plug, skip this step.
3. Wait five minutes for motor to cool The safety switch will not stay in while hot.
4. Press red reset button underneath Find the small red button on the flat bottom. Press lightly until it clicks and stays in. If it pops out again, wait and try once more.
5. Run cold water and test switch Turn cold water on first, then the switch. If still silent, check your home breaker box for a tripped switch.
